key_insight: DistSeal shows that watermarking inside a generative model's latent space—trained post-hoc—yields effective, low-overhead, less-visible watermarks that work for both diffusion and autoregressive generators.
problem_solved: Existing watermarking methods operate in pixel space and introduce extra computation and visible artifacts; this paper addresses how to embed robust watermarks earlier in the pipeline to reduce artifacts and cost while remaining model-agnostic.
method: Train lightweight encoder/decoder watermark modules post-hoc in the model's latent space (no retraining of the base generator).
Insert watermark signals into latents during generation (pre-decoding/denoising) so they propagate to pixels while preserving image quality.
Design a unified DistSeal training objective for both diffusion and autoregressive latents that balances detectability, visual fidelity, and robustness to common perturbations.
impact: Practitioners can retrofit existing generative models with efficient, low-impact provenance signals—improving detection/IP protection and reducing visual degradation and compute compared with pixel-space methods.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline diagram: pixel-space watermarking vs latent-space (DistSeal) watermarking showing where the watermark is inserted.
Architecture sketch of DistSeal encoder/decoder interacting with diffusion and autoregressive latents.
Bar chart comparing compute overhead and perceptual quality (e.g., FID or LPIPS) for pixel vs latent watermarking.
Robustness plot (ROC or detection accuracy) under common image perturbations (compression, crop, noise).
paper_title: Learning to Watermark in the Latent Space of Generative Models
paper_authors: Sylvestre-Alvise Rebuffi, Tuan Tran, Valeriu Lacatusu, Pierre Fernandez, Tomáš Souček
